summary: RED is genuinely causal and GREEN closes exactly that reason: a durable issued/outbox row surviving a rejected journal append now halts admission, refuses a pre-bound queued fold through the existing `creator snapshot export failed: not-active` path, and refuses later close binding with existing `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` until fresh authenticated recovery rebuilds the registration with `operationAdmissionHalted: false` (v3-live.ts:7296 is the only clearing site). The RED branch and its token remain live in the fixture, so a regression to close-advancement still fails the test. Scope is preserved: only `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts` internals plus tests-only fixture seams change; no wire/schema/API/dependency/authority/threshold/product-config edit, no in-process repair, no retirement-boundary relaxation, no campaign or D.110a run; the `-318`→`-317` D.110c-a repair keeps an exact `toBe` plus the exact reference-count assertion, so boundedness is not weakened. Two P1s block closure: (1) making close key on `operationAdmissionHalted` inherits a pre-existing setter on the provably pre-durable capacity arm, so with an operation-admission policy configured an ordinary `maxEpochBytes` exhaustion — the normal trigger to close and roll the epoch — now silently wedges the room until deactivation and recovery; (2) the retained roster omits the issuance/outbox/rebase, AHE-rollback, and snapshot gates this slice's own freeze names, which are exactly the fault-injection suites whose fold/close paths the broadened halt can flip.

findings.title: Pre-durable capacity rejection with a policy reservation now wedges creator close
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:5647-5653 sets `capacityRejected` and throws from inside `commitOutsideTransaction` before the store reaches `#commitCandidate` (packages/storage-node/src/internal/node-issuance-store.ts:600-603), so nothing is durably committed; but the throw follows `buildAndSign`, so `signerResolved` is already true (v3-live.ts:5635-5638). The catch at v3-live.ts:5685-5689 therefore skips `releaseOperationReservation` and sets `registration.operationAdmissionHalted = true` whenever `reservation !== undefined`, i.e. whenever the public `operationAdmissionPolicy` input is configured (v3-live.ts:4146-4166). GREEN then makes that flag refuse close at v3-live.ts:6985 (`creatorCloseRegistration`) and v3-live.ts:6655 (queued `stageClosedBlueprintEpoch` recheck). `issueLocal` pre-checks only vertex count (v3-live.ts:5883); byte capacity is never checked before `reserveOperation` (v3-live.ts:5621) and `hasGraphCapacity` fails on `maxEpochBytes` exhaustion (v3-live.ts:3621-3626).
findings.impact: In any deployment configuring `operationAdmissionPolicy`, filling an epoch to `maxEpochBytes` — the designed trigger to close and roll over — leaves the plane halted although no issuance transaction committed. `creatorCloseRegistration()` then returns undefined (bind returns `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE`) and a pre-bound close fails at the fold recheck, so the room can no longer close and requires a full deactivate plus authenticated recovery cycle. The caller sees only `v3 local issue graph is at capacity`, identical to the benign early return at line 5884, so the wedge is silent. This is new behavior: pre-GREEN the flag blocked admission only and close still advanced.
findings.required_action: In the `issueOneVertex` catch, treat the self-raised pre-commit capacity arm as definitely non-durable: release the reservation and do not halt when `capacityRejected` is true (e.g. `if ((!signerResolved && !terminalTransactionStarted) || capacityRejected) releaseOperationReservation(reservation); else if (reservation !== undefined || issuanceOutcomeUnknown) ...`). `capacityRejected` can only be set inside `commitOutsideTransaction` before a candidate reaches the store, including the terminal path at line 5662 where `terminalTransactionStarted` is still false, so it is always pre-durable. Add one focused case: policy configured, byte-capacity rejection, plane still closable. No API, wire, or configuration change.

findings.title: Retained roster omits issuance/outbox/rebase, AHE-rollback, and snapshot gates named by this slice's freeze
findings.evidence: The D.110c-0c1b freeze requires retaining "D.110c-0c1a carrier, E5-01 admission/recovery, Phase-6a successor recovery/adoption, issuance/outbox/rebase, AHE rollback, snapshot, D.109 reclamation, exact-owner static gates, and the D.110c-a/b hot path" (docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:96322-96325). The accepted retained command in .logs/d110c-0c1b-green-0873dfd0/commands.md selects nine files covering only 0c1b, E5-01, three Phase-6a suites, D.109d reclamation, D.110c-0c1a, D.110c-a, and D.110c-b. The named-but-unrun suites exist: tests/phase-3g-v3-rebase-outbox-red.test.ts, tests/phase-3a1b-p2-outbox-publication-contract.test.ts, tests/phase-6b-issuance-retention-red.test.ts, tests/phase-6b-ahe-reclamation-red.test.ts, tests/phase-4b-v3-live-snapshot-composition-red.test.ts.
findings.impact: GREEN changed `committedFailure()` (v3-live.ts:5703-5711) from halting only when a reservation existed to halting unconditionally, and made that halt refuse fold and close. Suites that inject a post-commit local-issue journal or graph failure and then stage a blueprint fold, export a snapshot, or close now traverse the new `v3 blueprint fold requires live recovery` / `CREATOR_CLOSE_UNAVAILABLE` paths instead of their previous success paths. No evidence in the GREEN root shows whether those suites still pass, so an executable regression among the changed file's own consumers would be undetected at closure.
findings.required_action: Run the named retained suites against the GREEN tree and record their reporter JSON in the evidence root, or record an explicit per-suite disposition stating why each is unaffected by the unconditional committed-failure halt and the close/fold refusal. Do not broaden the code change.

findings.title: Focused GREEN proves less than the frozen GREEN clause for the post-recovery plane
findings.evidence: The frozen GREEN requires that after recovery the product "complete genuine 0→1 close/adoption, restart/reopen, genuine 1→2 close/adoption, and continued issue/publish after epoch 2" and "Assert no duplicate journal/graph/application entry, no skipped sequence, no hidden pending row, the exact carrier boundary and non-null continuation, exact state digest, and exact operation count" (plan lines 96301-96308), and that neither refusal changes durable head or snapshot (96293-96296). In tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1b/committed-issuance-recovery-contract.ts the GREEN path is the catch at lines 229-253, asserting only the repeat-close message, `secondIssue` admission-rejected with row delta 0, one target row, and `recoveredSequenceDelta === 1`. `fixture.advancePendingSuccessor()` and `fixture.attemptCurrentSuccessorClose()` (lines 222-226) are reachable only on the RED branch, and no `inspectDurableHead()` comparison is taken after the refusal. The plan's GREEN narrative (96396-96405) was rewritten to the weaker delivered claim without recording that reduction.
findings.impact: The slice's central remedial claim — that after authenticated recovery the reconciled room can actually close again — is inferred rather than executed, and durable-head/snapshot invariance across the two refusals is unasserted. Static reading of packages/node/src/internal/creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:104-133 supports the claim (the recovered row regains the current anchor/epoch and in-graph membership, so the boundary is dense), so this is an evidence gap rather than a demonstrated defect.
findings.required_action: Disposition only. Either add the post-recovery close/adoption assertion to the focused test, or amend the frozen clause in the plan to state explicitly that post-recovery close continuity is carried by D.110c-0c1/0c and the retained D.110c-a/b hot path.

findings.title: Tests-only non-delegation and evidence fields are tautological rather than observed
findings.evidence: tests/fixtures/phase-6b-d110c-0c1b/committed-issuance-recovery-contract.ts:120 declares `const journalWriteDelegated = false` and never assigns it, so the guard at line 81 (`if (journalWriteDelegated) throw ...`) and the reported field can never fail. Similarly `assertCommittedFailure` (lines 93-105) returns hardcoded literals for every field; the real proof lives in the catch-block checks at lines 231-252 and in the decorator at lines 130-136, which throws without calling `store.appendAccepted`.
findings.impact: A reader of the reporter output or of `D110c0c1bRedEvidence` can mistake constant fields for observed measurements, and a future edit that made the decorator delegate the armed append would not be caught by the `journalWriteDelegated` guard. No current production or test outcome is wrong.
findings.required_action: Set `journalWriteDelegated` from the decorator (assign true on the delegating branch) or delete the field and rely on the structural non-delegation argument already recorded in the RED validation. No production change.
